results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies when landlord wants to permanently retire property from residential use, excluding health and safety removal cases.

If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires  
(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies when tenant habitually pays rent late or fails to pay after written Notice to Cease.

results.quoted_span:
If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to 
Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the 
tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to tenants residing on condition of employment by landlord as superintendent, janitor, or similar.

If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as 
a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three 
days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to tenants convicted of drug offenses, theft, or human trafficking related to the premises or allowing such persons to reside there.

No eviction suit may 
be brought more than two years after : the juvenile was found to be delinquent;

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish for new construction is required to pay relocation

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:

results.quoted_span:
Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available 
the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s 
agent. In addition, within three business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord must notify 
the tenant in writing of when and where the tenant can pick up the security deposit.

results.reason: all coverage conditions met
results.summary_plain: Your landlord must follow state laws about security deposits, including how they handle and disclose them.
results.summary_plain_es: Su arrendador debe cumplir con las leyes estatales sobre depósitos de seguridad, incluyendo cómo manejarlos y divulgarlos.
results.quoted_span:
Every landlord subject to the Truth in Renting Act, (N.J.S.A. 46:8-43 to 51), hereinafter 
the Act, is required to distribute one copy of the Truth in Renting Statement to each of their tenants 
within 30 days after it has been posted by the Department on its website and shall thereafter provide 
a copy of the most current statement to each new tenant at or prior to the time the tenant executes 
a lease for the rental unit.

results.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
results.penalty: Up to $500 for first offense, $750 for second, and $1,000 for subsequent offenses.

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartments, rooming and boarding homes.
results.summary_plain: In New Jersey, a landlord can only evict you for specific reasons like not paying rent, causing damage, or breaking lease rules, and must follow legal procedures.
results.summary_plain_es: En Nueva Jersey, un propietario solo puede desalojarte por razones específicas como no pagar el alquiler, causar daños o romper las reglas del contrato, y debe seguir procedimientos legales.
results.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to 
prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies when landlord wants to permanently retire property from residential use, excluding health and safety removal cases.
results.summary_plain: If your landlord wants to stop renting the building permanently, they must give you 18 months notice before suing to evict you and wait until your lease ends.
results.summary_plain_es: Si su casero quiere dejar de alquilar el edificio permanentemente, debe darle un aviso de 18 meses antes de demandar para desalojarlo y esperar hasta que termine su contrato.
results.quoted_span:
If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires  
(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies when tenant habitually pays rent late or fails to pay after written Notice to Cease.
results.summary_plain: If you keep paying rent late or not at all after being warned, your landlord can evict you with one month notice.
results.summary_plain_es: Si sigue pagando la renta tarde o no la paga después de una advertencia, su casero puede desalojarlo con un aviso de un mes.
results.quoted_span:
If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to 
Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the 
tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to tenants residing on condition of employment by landlord as superintendent, janitor, or similar.
results.summary_plain: If you live in your rental because you work for the landlord and your job ends, they can evict you with 3 days notice.
results.summary_plain_es: Si vive en su alquiler porque trabaja para el casero y su trabajo termina, pueden desalojarlo con un aviso de 3 días.
results.quoted_span:
If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as 
a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three 
days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to tenants convicted of drug offenses, theft, or human trafficking related to the premises or allowing such persons to reside there.

results.summary_plain_es: Puede ser desalojado si usted o alguien que permite vivir con usted ha sido condenado por ciertos delitos relacionados con la propiedad, pero el desalojo debe presentarse dentro de los dos años posteriores a la condena o liberación.

be brought more than two years after : the juvenile was found to be delinquent;

a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A.

including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to residential rental properties except one-family or two-family dwellings and licensees of the NJ Real Estate Commission who are not landlords.
results.summary_plain: Landlords in New Jersey cannot charge more than $50 for rental application fees, and this limit increases yearly with inflation.
results.summary_plain_es: Los propietarios en Nueva Jersey no pueden cobrar más de $50 por las tarifas de solicitud de alquiler, y este límite aumenta anualmente con la inflación.
results.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
results.penalty: Up to $500 for first offense, $750 for second, and $1,000 for subsequent offenses.

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartments, rooming and boarding homes.
results.summary_plain: In New Jersey, a landlord can only evict you for specific reasons like not paying rent, causing damage, or breaking lease rules, and must follow legal procedures.
results.summary_plain_es: En Nueva Jersey, un propietario solo puede desalojarte por razones específicas como no pagar el alquiler, causar daños o romper las reglas del contrato, y debe seguir procedimientos legales.
results.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to 
prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies when landlord wants to permanently retire property from residential use, excluding health and safety removal cases.
results.summary_plain: If your landlord wants to stop renting the building permanently, they must give you 18 months notice before suing to evict you and wait until your lease ends.
results.summary_plain_es: Si su casero quiere dejar de alquilar el edificio permanentemente, debe darle un aviso de 18 meses antes de demandar para desalojarlo y esperar hasta que termine su contrato.
results.quoted_span:
If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires  
(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies when tenant habitually pays rent late or fails to pay after written Notice to Cease.
results.summary_plain: If you keep paying rent late or not at all after being warned, your landlord can evict you with one month notice.
results.summary_plain_es: Si sigue pagando la renta tarde o no la paga después de una advertencia, su casero puede desalojarlo con un aviso de un mes.
results.quoted_span:
If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to 
Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the 
tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to tenants residing on condition of employment by landlord as superintendent, janitor, or similar.
results.summary_plain: If you live in your rental because you work for the landlord and your job ends, they can evict you with 3 days notice.
results.summary_plain_es: Si vive en su alquiler porque trabaja para el casero y su trabajo termina, pueden desalojarlo con un aviso de 3 días.
results.quoted_span:
If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as 
a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three 
days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to tenants convicted of drug offenses, theft, or human trafficking related to the premises or allowing such persons to reside there.
results.summary_plain: You can be evicted if you or someone you allow to live with you has been convicted of certain crimes related to the property, but eviction must be filed within two years of the conviction or release.
results.summary_plain_es: Puede ser desalojado si usted o alguien que permite vivir con usted ha sido condenado por ciertos delitos relacionados con la propiedad, pero el desalojo debe presentarse dentro de los dos años posteriores a la condena o liberación.
results.quoted_span:
No eviction suit may 
be brought more than two years after : the juvenile was found to be delinquent; 
conviction of the person; or after the person’s release fr om incarceration, whichever is 
later. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit 
for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(p)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to all rental properties except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
results.summary_plain: Your landlord cannot evict or punish you for asserting your rights or reporting problems in good faith.
results.summary_plain_es: Su propietario no puede desalojarlo ni castigarlo por hacer valer sus derechos o reportar problemas de buena fe.
results.quoted_span:
A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of 
a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 
2A:42-10.10).  The law against reprisal applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, 
including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.

if an appeal by a

results.summary_plain_es: Su arrendador debe darle un aviso adecuado antes de aumentar su renta, y el aumento no puede ser irrazonablemente alto.
results.quoted_span:
before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of 
an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent 
increase. This notice does not mean that the tenant must actually leave; the tenant has the right to 
remain as long as they pay any legal increase in rent. The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

results.summary_plain: If you have lived in your rental for at least 12 months, your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you and must state it in writing.
results.summary_plain_es: Si ha vivido en su alquiler por al menos 12 meses, su arrendador debe tener una razón válida para desalojarlo y debe indicarla por escrito.
results.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

results.reason: all coverage conditions met
results.summary_plain: In Los Angeles, landlords can only evict tenants for specific legal reasons like not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord or family needs to move in.
results.summary_plain_es: En Los Ángeles, los propietarios solo pueden desalojar a los inquilinos por razones legales específicas como no pagar la renta, incumplir el contrato o si el propietario o su familia necesitan mudarse.
results.quoted_span:
Legal Reasons for Eviction
Tenant is at-fault
Failure to pay rent
Failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement
Creating a nuisance or causing damage to the rental unit
Using the rental unit for an illegal purpose
Failure to renew a similar rental agreement
Failure to provide the landlord with reasonable access to the rental unit
The person at the end of the lease term is a subtenant not approved by the landlord
Tenant is not at-fault
The owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit
A resident manager will move into the rental unit
Demolition and permanent removal from the rental market
Government order
Conversion to affordable housing

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to Protected Units that are residential dwelling units subject to rent or price control or rented by lower income households within the past five years, or withdrawn under Ellis Act within past 10 years.
results.summary_plain: If your landlord wants to evict you to demolish your unit for new construction, they must notify the city, give you written notice, and pay you relocation assistance that is higher for lower income tenants.
results.summary_plain_es: Si su arrendador quiere desalojarlo para demoler su unidad y construir algo nuevo, debe notificar a la ciudad, darle un aviso por escrito y pagarle asistencia para la reubicación, que es mayor para inquilinos de bajos ingresos.
results.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code Sections 151.22-151.28, 165.03.I(1); Ordinances #188481 and #188482
results.quoted_span:
A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish for new construction is required to pay relocation 
assistance and to file a Declaration of Intent to Evict or Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units From Rental 
Housing Use with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) prior to evicting tenants from units 
covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).
results.penalty: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances for failure to comply with RPO.

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.

The proposed ordinance bans the sale, licensing, and use of an algorithmic device to set rental rates or 
occupancy levels for residential rental properties. Algorithmic devices are a software or product that uses 
or incorporates one or more algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data concerning 
rental rates, occupancy levels, or other information regarding the leasing of residential rental property to 
advise, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or occupancy levels.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:

(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

results.quoted_span:
The proposed ordinance bans the sale, licensing, and use of an algorithmic device to set rental rates or 
occupancy levels for residential rental properties. Algorithmic devices are a software or product that uses 
or incorporates one or more algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data concerning 
rental rates, occupancy levels, or other information regarding the leasing of residential rental property to 
advise, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or occupancy levels.

algorithmic device to a landlord.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

results.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
results.quoted_span:
If you own rental property in the City of Los Angeles, it may be subject to the
Just Cause Ordinance
(JCO).  It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

results.summary_plain: If your landlord wants to evict you to demolish your unit for new construction, they must notify the city, give you written notice, and pay you relocation assistance that is higher for lower income tenants.
results.summary_plain_es: Si su arrendador quiere desalojarlo para demoler su unidad y construir algo nuevo, debe notificar a la ciudad, darle un aviso por escrito y pagarle asistencia para la reubicación, que es mayor para inquilinos de bajos ingresos.
results.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code Sections 151.22-151.28, 165.03.I(1); Ordinances #188481 and #188482
results.quoted_span:
A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish for new construction is required to pay relocation 
assistance and to file a Declaration of Intent to Evict or Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units From Rental 
Housing Use with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) prior to evicting tenants from units 
covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).
results.penalty: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances for failure to comply with RPO.

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to

results.summary_plain_es: Si su casero quiere dejar de alquilar el edificio permanentemente, debe darle un aviso de 18 meses antes de demandar para desalojarlo y esperar hasta que termine su contrato.
results.quoted_span:
If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires  
(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

results.quoted_span:
If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to 
Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the 
tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as 
a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three 
days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

be brought more than two years after : the juvenile was found to be delinquent;

before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of 
an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent 
increase. This notice does not mean that the tenant must actually leave; the tenant has the right to 
remain as long as they pay any legal increase in rent. The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

results.quoted_span:
before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of 
an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent 
increase. This notice does not mean that the tenant must actually leave; the tenant has the right to 
remain as long as they pay any legal increase in rent. The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:

(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires  
(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the

a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three

results.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Ellis Implementation Ordinance
results.quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction. The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market. results.quoted_span:
At its regular meeting on October 16, 2025, the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board 
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026. The 2026 AGA of 1.0% represents 65% of the increase in the Consumer 
Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers in the Bay Area during the period from July 1, 
2024 - June 30, 2025, which was 1.5% as posted by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:

(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

results.quoted_span:
The proposed ordinance bans the sale, licensing, and use of an algorithmic device to set rental rates or 
occupancy levels for residential rental properties. Algorithmic devices are a software or product that uses 
or incorporates one or more algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data concerning 
rental rates, occupancy levels, or other information regarding the leasing of residential rental property to 
advise, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or occupancy levels.

results.reason: all coverage conditions met
results.summary_plain: In San Diego, landlords cannot use or obtain software that uses competitor data to set or recommend rental prices or occupancy levels. Tenants can take legal action if this happens.

results.quoted_span:
(a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an
algorithmic device to a landlord.
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
results.penalty: Tenants may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. Prevailing tenants recover costs and attorney’s fees.

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply

exceeds $50.
results.penalty: Up to $500 for first offense, $750 for second, and $1,000 for subsequent offenses.

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartments, rooming and boarding homes.
results.summary_plain: In New Jersey, a landlord can only evict you for specific reasons like not paying rent, causing damage, or breaking lease rules, and must follow legal procedures.
results.summary_plain_es: En Nueva Jersey, un propietario solo puede desalojarte por razones específicas como no pagar el alquiler, causar daños o romper las reglas del contrato, y debe seguir procedimientos legales.
results.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to 
prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies when landlord wants to permanently retire property from residential use, excluding health and safety removal cases.
results.summary_plain: If your landlord wants to stop renting the building permanently, they must give you 18 months notice before suing to evict you and wait until your lease ends.
results.summary_plain_es: Si su casero quiere dejar de alquilar el edificio permanentemente, debe darle un aviso de 18 meses antes de demandar para desalojarlo y esperar hasta que termine su contrato.
results.quoted_span:
If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires  
(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies when tenant habitually pays rent late or fails to pay after written Notice to Cease.
results.summary_plain: If you keep paying rent late or not at all after being warned, your landlord can evict you with one month notice.
results.summary_plain_es: Si sigue pagando la renta tarde o no la paga después de una advertencia, su casero puede desalojarlo con un aviso de un mes.
results.quoted_span:
If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to 
Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the 
tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to tenants residing on condition of employment by landlord as superintendent, janitor, or similar.
results.summary_plain: If you live in your rental because you work for the landlord and your job ends, they can evict you with 3 days notice.
results.summary_plain_es: Si vive en su alquiler porque trabaja para el casero y su trabajo termina, pueden desalojarlo con un aviso de 3 días.
results.quoted_span:
If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as 
a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three 
days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to tenants convicted of drug offenses, theft, or human trafficking related to the premises or allowing such persons to reside there.
results.summary_plain: You can be evicted if you or someone you allow to live with you has been convicted of certain crimes related to the property, but eviction must be filed within two years of the conviction or release.
results.summary_plain_es: Puede ser desalojado si usted o alguien que permite vivir con usted ha sido condenado por ciertos delitos relacionados con la propiedad, pero el desalojo debe presentarse dentro de los dos años posteriores a la condena o liberación.
results.quoted_span:
No eviction suit may 
be brought more than two years after : the juvenile was found to be delinquent; 
conviction of the person; or after the person’s release fr om incarceration, whichever is 
later. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:

(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to

If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires  
(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to 
Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the 
tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as 
a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three 
days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

results.summary_plain_es: Puede ser desalojado si usted o alguien que permite vivir con usted ha sido condenado por ciertos delitos relacionados con la propiedad, pero el desalojo debe presentarse dentro de los dos años posteriores a la condena o liberación.

No eviction suit may 
be brought more than two years after : the juvenile was found to be delinquent; 
conviction of the person; or after the person’s release fr om incarceration, whichever is

for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(p)).

a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 
2A:42-10.10).  The law against reprisal applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, 
including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:

(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay

use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months

(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

The proposed ordinance bans the sale, licensing, and use of an algorithmic device to set rental rates or 
occupancy levels for residential rental properties. Algorithmic devices are a software or product that uses 
or incorporates one or more algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data concerning 
rental rates, occupancy levels, or other information regarding the leasing of residential rental property to 
advise, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or occupancy levels.

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

The proposed ordinance bans the sale, licensing, and use of an algorithmic device to set rental rates or 
occupancy levels for residential rental properties. Algorithmic devices are a software or product that uses

advise, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or occupancy levels.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.

reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:

(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to

results.reason: coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies when landlord wants to permanently retire property from residential use, excluding health and safety removal cases.
results.summary_plain: If your landlord wants to stop renting the building permanently, they must give you 18 months notice before suing to evict you and wait until your lease ends.
results.summary_plain_es: Si su casero quiere dejar de alquilar el edificio permanentemente, debe darle un aviso de 18 meses antes de demandar para desalojarlo y esperar hasta que termine su contrato.
results.quoted_span:
If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires  
(N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the

a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three 
days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

results.summary_plain: San Diego bans software that uses secret competitor data to set or suggest rents or occupancy levels for rental homes.
results.summary_plain_es: San Diego prohíbe el software que utiliza datos secretos de competidores para establecer o sugerir rentas o niveles de ocupación para viviendas en alquiler.
results.citation: San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 11, Sections 98.1101-98.1104
results.quoted_span:
The proposed ordinance bans the sale, licensing, and use of an algorithmic device to set rental rates or 
occupancy levels for residential rental properties. Algorithmic devices are a software or product that uses 
or incorporates one or more algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data concerning 
rental rates, occupancy levels, or other information regarding the leasing of residential rental property to 
advise, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or occupancy levels.

results.reason: all coverage conditions met
results.summary_plain: In San Diego, landlords cannot use or obtain software that uses competitor data to set or recommend rental prices or occupancy levels. Tenants can take legal action if this happens.
results.summary_plain_es: En San Diego, los propietarios no pueden usar ni obtener software que utilice datos de competidores para establecer o recomendar precios de alquiler o niveles de ocupación. Los inquilinos pueden tomar acciones legales si esto ocurre.
results.quoted_span:
(a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an
algorithmic device to a landlord.
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
results.penalty: Tenants may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. Prevailing tenants recover costs and attorney’s fees.

results.summary_plain: In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores.
results.summary_plain_es: En California, los propietarios no pueden discriminar injustamente basado en la fuente de sus ingresos o historial crediticio. Si tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno, deben considerar su capacidad de pago usando pruebas alternativas, no solo puntajes de crédito.
results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.

reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay

(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s

(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

The proposed ordinance bans the sale, licensing, and use of an algorithmic device to set rental rates or 
occupancy levels for residential rental properties. Algorithmic devices are a software or product that uses

rental rates, occupancy levels, or other information regarding the leasing of residential rental property to 
advise, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or occupancy levels.

results.quoted_span:
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
(ii) If the applicant elects to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s
reasonable ability to pay pursuant to clause (i), the housing provider shall do both of the following:
(I) Provide the applicant reasonable time to respond with that alternative evidence.
(II) Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.

results.quoted_span:
The proposed ordinance bans the sale, licensing, and use of an algorithmic device to set rental rates or 
occupancy levels for residential rental properties. Algorithmic devices are a software or product that uses 
or incorporates one or more algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data concerning 
rental rates, occupancy levels, or other information regarding the leasing of residential rental property to 
advise, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or occupancy levels.

(a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an
algorithmic device to a landlord.
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
results.penalty: Tenants may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. Prevailing tenants recover costs and attorney’s fees.
